raw.retained_raw_text: {"schema_version":"chat_response_v1","response_type":"answer","answer_text":"The light-dependent reactions convert light energy into chemical energy stored in energy carriers, and these carriers transport that energy to the Calvin cycle. The light-dependent reactions use light to temporarily store energy in energy carriers [ev_005] [ev_008]. Photosystems absorb light and use electron transport chains to convert energy into the chemical energy of ATP and NADPH [ev_002]. These energy-carrying molecules travel into the stroma, where the Calvin cycle reactions take place [ev_007]. The Calvin cycle then uses the energy in ATP and NADPH to convert CO2-derived molecules into G3P [ev_010]. The carriers are described as \"full\" when they carry energy from the light-dependent reactions, and they return as \"empty\" carriers to the light-dependent reactions to obtain more energy after the energy is released [ev_001] [ev_005]. The Calvin cycle is the set of reactions that use the energy stored by the light-dependent reactions to form glucose and other carbohydrate molecules [ev_011].","short_answer":"Light-dependent reactions store light energy in ATP and NADPH [ev_008] [ev_002], which travel to the Calvin cycle in the stroma to power carbohydrate synthesis [ev_007] [ev_011].","citations":["ev_001","ev_002","ev_005","ev_007","ev_008","ev_010","ev_011"],"refusal_reason":null,"follow_up_questions":[],"confidence":0.85,"tutor_question":null,"learner_attempt_evaluation":null}
